How this is calculated

This is a gameplay model with fixed design assumptions, not a calibrated forecast. It does not use live opinion polls.

  1. The starting vote shares blend 2024 constituency results (80%), 2019 notional results on the same boundaries (17%) and 2017 country-level results (3%). Missing historical data falls back to the latest local distribution. Scenario affiliation transfers are applied to the 2024 baseline; the historical result panel stays unchanged.
  2. Candidate adjustments combine political outlook (up to ±2 points), career (up to ±0.75), university (0 to +0.35) and shared upbringing region or nation (+0.75). Their sum is limited to −4 to +3 points before vote shares are normalised. These are game rules, not measured effects on voters.
  3. The estimated lead over the strongest rival is converted to a probability using a normal distribution with an assumed uncertainty scale of 11.5–15.5 percentage points. Displayed probabilities are rounded and capped at 1–99%.
  4. Independent candidates use the party associated with their chosen outlook as a reference, then receive 80% of that reference probability. This is a gameplay rule; their displayed margin describes the reference contest.

Historical data: House of Commons Library election results and Parliament notional results, as embedded in this file. Local political outlook is inferred from party support, not a voter survey. No validation against held-out elections is supplied with this model.
